translation_en: Abu Nuaim narrated to us; Shayban narrated to us, from Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “When one of you drinks, let him not breathe into the vessel. When one of you urinates, let him not touch his private part with his right hand, and when one of you cleans himself after relieving himself, let him not use his right hand.”

Abu Asim and Abu Nuaim narrated to us; they said: Azrah ibn Thabit narrated to us: Thumamah ibn Abdullah informed me that Anas used to breathe into the vessel twice or three times, and he maintained that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to breathe three times.

Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Layla, who said: Hudhayfah was in al-Mada'in and asked for water. A landowner brought him a silver cup, so Hudhayfah threw it at him and said: I only threw it because I had forbidden him and he did not stop. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade us silk, brocade, and drinking from gold and silver vessels, and he said: “Those are for them in this world, and they are for you in the Hereafter.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us; Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abi Layla, who said: We went out with Hudhayfah, and he mentioned the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as saying: “Do not drink from gold and silver vessels, and do not wear silk or brocade, for they are for them in this world and for you in the Hereafter.”

Ismail narrated to us: Malik ibn Anas narrated to me, from Nafi, from Zayd ibn Abdullah ibn Umar, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, from Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever drinks from a silver vessel is only swallowing the fire of Hell into his belly.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Abu Awanah narrated to us, from al-Ashath ibn Sulaym, from Muawiyah ibn Suwayd ibn Muqarrin, from al-Bara ibn Azib, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded us to do seven things and forbade us from seven. He commanded us to visit the sick, follow funeral processions, invoke Allah's mercy for the sneezer, accept invitations, spread greetings of peace, support the wronged, and fulfill the oath of one who swears. He forbade us gold rings, drinking from silver—or he said silver vessels—cushioned horse cloths, Qassiy garments, and wearing silk, brocade, and thick silk.

Amr ibn Abbas narrated to me; Abd al-Rahman narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Salim Abu al-Nadr, from Umayr, the freedman of Umm al-Fadl, from Umm al-Fadl, that they were uncertain about the Prophet's fast on the Day of Arafah, so a cup of milk was sent to him and he drank it.

Said ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us; Abu Ghassan narrated to us, saying: Abu Hazim narrated to me, from Sahl ibn Sad, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A woman from the Arabs was mentioned to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, so he told Abu Usayd al-Saidi to send for her. He did so, and she came and stayed among the gardens of Banu Saidah. The Prophet went to her and entered upon her, and found her with her head bowed. When he spoke to her, she said: “I seek refuge in Allah from you.” He replied: “I grant you refuge from me.” They asked her: “Do you know who this is?” She said: “No.” They said: “This is the Messenger of Allah, who came to propose to you.” She said: “I was more wretched than that.” That day the Prophet went and sat in the shelter of Banu Saidah with his companions, then said: “Give us a drink, Sahl.” I brought them this cup and served them from it. Sahl later brought out that same cup, and we drank from it. He said that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz later asked him for it as a gift, and he gave it to him.

Al-Hasan ibn Mudrik narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to me; Abu Awanah informed us, from Asim al-Ahwal, who said: I saw the Prophet's cup with Anas ibn Malik. It had cracked, so he repaired it with silver. He said it was a fine, broad cup made of valuable wood. Anas said: I served the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, from this cup more times than I can count. Ibn Sirin said: It had an iron ring, and Anas wanted to replace it with a gold or silver ring. Abu Talhah told him: “Do not alter anything the Messenger of Allah made.” So he left it as it was.

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us, from al-Amash, who said: Salim ibn Abi al-Jad narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both, this hadith. He said: I saw myself with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when the time for the afternoon prayer came and we had no water except a little that remained. It was put in a vessel and brought to the Prophet. He put his hand into it, spread his fingers, then said: “Come, those who perform ablution; the blessing is from Allah.” I saw water gushing from between his fingers. The people performed ablution and drank. I made sure to take as much as I could into my stomach, for I knew it was a blessing. I asked Jabir: How many were you that day? He said: One thousand four hundred. Amr also reported it from Jabir. Husayn and Amr ibn Murrah reported from Salim, from Jabir: fifteen hundred. Said ibn al-Musayyab also reported it from Jabir.

Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi narrated to us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, said the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “No affliction befalls a Muslim except that Allah expiates some of his sins by it, even a thorn that pricks him.”

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to me; Abd al-Malik ibn Amr narrated to us; Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Halhalah, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Said al-Khudri and from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “No fatigue, illness, worry, grief, harm, or distress befalls a Muslim—even a thorn that pricks him—except that Allah expiates some of his sins by it.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Sad, from Abdullah ibn Kab, from his father, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The example of a believer is like a tender plant in a field: the wind bends it one way and then straightens it another. The example of a hypocrite is like a cedar tree that remains upright until it is uprooted all at once.” Zakariyya said: Sad narrated to me; Ibn Kab narrated to us, from his father Kab, from the Prophet, the same report.

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fulayh narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from Hilal ibn Ali, of Banu Amir ibn Luayy, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The example of a believer is like a tender plant: from whatever direction the wind comes, it bends it. When it becomes upright, affliction makes it sway again. But the wicked person is like a firmly rooted, rigid cedar tree, remaining upright until Allah breaks it whenever He wills.”

Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Malik informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sasaa, who said: I heard Said ibn Yasar Abu al-Hubab say: I heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “When Allah intends good for someone, He afflicts him.”

Qabisah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Amash. Bishr ibn Muhammad narrated to me; Abdullah informed us; Shu'bah informed us, from al-Amash, from Abu Wail, from Masruq, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: I have never seen anyone suffer pain more severely than the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him: I visited the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, during his illness when he was suffering a severe fever. I said: You are suffering a severe fever. I said: That is because you will have a double reward. He said: “Yes. No Muslim is afflicted by harm except that Allah removes his sins from him as leaves fall from a tree.”

Abdan narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-Amash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah, who said: I visited the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was suffering fever. I said: Messenger of Allah, you are suffering a severe fever. He said: “Yes, I suffer fever as severely as two men among you.” I said: Is that because you will have a double reward? He said: “Yes, that is so. No Muslim is afflicted by harm, even a thorn or anything greater, except that Allah expiates his sins by it, as a tree sheds its leaves.”

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us; Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wail, from Abu Musa al-Ashari, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Feed the hungry, visit the sick, and free the captive.”

Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Ashath ibn Sulaym informed me: I heard Muawiyah ibn Suwayd ibn Muqarrin, from al-Bara ibn Azib, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded us to do seven things and forbade us from seven. He forbade us gold rings, wearing silk, brocade, thick silk, Qassiy garments, and cushioned horse cloths; and he commanded us to follow funeral processions, visit the sick, and spread greetings of peace.

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir, who heard Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: I became seriously ill, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to visit me, with Abu Bakr walking beside him. They found me unconscious. The Prophet performed ablution, then poured some of his ablution water over me, and I regained consciousness. I said: Messenger of Allah, what should I do with my wealth? How should I distribute my wealth? He did not answer me until the verse of inheritance was revealed.

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Imran Abu Bakr, who said: Ata ibn Abi Rabah narrated to me: Ibn Abbas said to me, “Shall I show you a woman from the people of Paradise?” I said, “Yes.” He said: “This black woman came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: ‘I suffer seizures and become uncovered, so pray to Allah for me.’ He said: ‘If you wish, be patient and Paradise will be yours; or, if you wish, I will pray to Allah to restore your health.’ She said: ‘I will be patient.’ Then she said: ‘I become uncovered, so pray to Allah that I will not become uncovered.’ So he prayed for her.” Muhammad narrated to us; Makhlad informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata informed me that he saw that woman, Umm Zufar, a tall black woman, near the covering of the Kaaba.

Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Had narrated to me, from Amr, the freedman of al-Muttalib, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “Allah said: When I test My servant by taking his two beloved [eyes] and he remains patient, I will compensate him with Paradise.” He meant his eyes. Ashath ibn Jabir and Abu Hilal also reported it from Anas, from the Prophet.

Qutaybah narrated to us, from Malik, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aishah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, arrived in Medina, Abu Bakr and Bilal, may Allah be pleased with them both, became ill with fever. I went in to them and said: “Father, how are you feeling? Bilal, how are you feeling?” When Abu Bakr was overcome by fever, he would say: “Every man wakes among his family, while death is nearer to him than his sandal strap.” When Bilal's fever subsided, he would say: “Would that I knew whether I will spend a night in a valley around me, with idhkhir and jalil grasses, and whether I will one day reach the waters of Majannah, and whether Shamah and Tufayl will appear to me.” Aishah said: I went to the Messenger of Allah and told him. He said: “O Allah, make Medina as beloved to us as Mecca, or even more; make it healthy for us, bless our mudd and sa, and move its fever to al-Juhfah.”

Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Asim informed me: I heard Abu Uthman narrate from Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a daughter of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent for him while he was with the Prophet, Saad, and Ubayy. We thought she said: “My daughter is at the point of death, so come to us.” He sent her greetings and said: “To Allah belongs what He takes and what He gives, and everything has an appointed term with Him. Let her seek reward and be patient.” She sent again, adjuring him to come. The Prophet stood, and we stood with him. The child was lifted into the Prophet's lap, and her breath was rattling. The Prophet's eyes overflowed with tears. Saad said: “What is this, Messenger of Allah?” He replied: “This is mercy that Allah places in the hearts of whichever of His servants He wills. Allah shows mercy only to those of His servants who are merciful.”

Mual la ibn Asad narrated to us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Mukhtar narrated to us; Khalid narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, visited a Bedouin who was ill. Whenever the Prophet visited a sick person, he would say to him: “No harm; it will be a purification, if Allah wills.” The man replied: “A purification? No! It is a fever boiling—or surging—in an old man, which will bring him to the graves.” The Prophet said: “Then so be it.”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: A Jewish boy who served the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, became ill. The Prophet visited him and said: “Accept Islam.” The boy accepted Islam. Said ibn al-Musayyab reported from his father: When Abu Talib was near death, the Prophet came to him.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us; Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father informed me, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her: Some people came to visit the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, during his illness. He led them in prayer while sitting, but they prayed standing, so he gestured to them to sit. When he finished, he said: “The imam is appointed to be followed. When he bows, bow; when he rises, rise. If he prays sitting, then pray sitting.” Abu Abdullah said: Al-Humaydi said this hadith has been abrogated, because the last time the Prophet prayed, he prayed sitting while the people behind him stood.

Al-Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; al-Juayd informed us, from Aishah bint Sad, that her father said: I became seriously ill in Mecca, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to visit me. I said: Prophet of Allah, I am leaving wealth, and I have only one daughter. Shall I bequeath two-thirds of my wealth and leave one-third? He said: “No.” I said: Half, and leave half? He said: “No.” I said: A third, and leave her two-thirds? He said: “A third, and a third is a lot.” Then he placed his hand on my forehead, passed it over my face and stomach, and said: “O Allah, heal Sad and complete his emigration for him.” I have continued to feel its coolness on my liver—as it seems to me—right up to this day.

Qutaybah narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from al-Harith ibn Suwayd, who said: Abdullah ibn Masud said: I visited the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was suffering fever. I touched him with my hand and said: Messenger of Allah, you are suffering a severe fever. The Messenger of Allah said: “Yes, I suffer fever as severely as two men among you.” I said: That is because you will have a double reward. The Messenger of Allah said: “Yes.” Then he said: “No Muslim is afflicted by harm, illness, or anything else except that Allah removes his sins from him as a tree sheds its leaves.”
